SITE.name: Behold
SITE.tagline: The life of Jesus Christ, told through every soul He touched.
SITE.dedication: Made with love, for my mother.

VERSES.t: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Be still, and know that I am God.
It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
We love him, because he first loved us.
I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.
I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

Neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain.
Behold, I make all things new.
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: the LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: the LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

GOSPELS.name: Matthew
GOSPELS.who: A tax collector called from his booth in Capernaum.
GOSPELS.audience: Written for a Jewish audience, it shows Jesus as the Messiah foretold by the prophets — the Son of David, the true King of Israel.

open.t: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

GOSPELS.name: Mark
GOSPELS.who: John Mark, companion of Peter, recording the apostle’s preaching.
GOSPELS.audience: The shortest and swiftest Gospel. Its favourite word is “straightway” — a life of urgent action, poured out in service.

open.t: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

GOSPELS.name: Luke
GOSPELS.who: A physician and careful historian, travelling companion of Paul.
GOSPELS.audience: The most detailed account, with a tender eye for the poor, for women, for outsiders — the Son of Man who came to seek the lost.

open.t: That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.

GOSPELS.name: John
GOSPELS.who: “The disciple whom Jesus loved,” fisherman and eyewitness.
GOSPELS.audience: Soaring like its eagle, it begins before time itself. Seven signs and seven “I AM” sayings reveal the Word made flesh.

open.t: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verse.t: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth.
Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

ACTS.title: The Kingdom Is at Hand
ACTS.places: Nazareth · Capernaum · The Sea of Galilee

verse.t: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
He stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem.

ACTS.title: Behold, Thy King
ACTS.places: Bethany · The Temple · The Upper Room

verse.t: Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.
But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.

ACTS.title: He Is Risen
ACTS.places: The Garden Tomb · Emmaus · Galilee · Olivet
ACTS.era: The First Day of the Week

verse.t: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Zechariah
ENCOUNTERS.role: An aged priest of the course of Abijah
ENCOUNTERS.text: While burning incense in the holy place, the old priest is met by the angel Gabriel: his barren wife Elizabeth will bear a son who will prepare the way of the Lord. Doubting, Zechariah is struck silent until the day his son is named John.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Mary of Nazareth
ENCOUNTERS.role: A young virgin betrothed to Joseph
ENCOUNTERS.text: Gabriel greets a young woman in an obscure Galilean village: she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear the Son of the Highest, whose kingdom shall have no end. Her answer is the most complete surrender in Scripture.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Elizabeth
ENCOUNTERS.text: When Mary enters her home, the child in Elizabeth’s womb leaps for joy, and she is filled with the Holy Spirit. Mary responds with the Magnificat — “My soul doth magnify the Lord.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Joseph
ENCOUNTERS.text: A just man, Joseph resolves to quietly set Mary aside — until an angel speaks to him in a dream. He rises and obeys, taking Mary as his wife and giving the child His name.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Shepherds
ENCOUNTERS.role: Keeping watch over their flock by night
ENCOUNTERS.text: The first to hear the news are not kings but labourers in the dark. The glory of the Lord shines round about them, a multitude of heavenly host sings, and they hurry to find the baby lying in a manger.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Simeon
ENCOUNTERS.role: A just and devout man awaiting Israel’s consolation
ENCOUNTERS.text: Promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Lord’s Christ, Simeon takes the forty-day-old infant in his arms — and warns Mary that a sword will pierce her own soul.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Anna
ENCOUNTERS.text: A widow who never left the temple, serving God with fasting and prayer night and day. Seeing the child, she gives thanks and speaks of Him to everyone looking for redemption.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: She… spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Magi
ENCOUNTERS.text: Guided by a star, scholars from a distant land travel to worship a child-king. They fall down before Him and open their treasures — gold, frankincense and myrrh — then, warned in a dream, return home another way.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: We have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Herod the Great
ENCOUNTERS.text: Threatened by news of a newborn King, Herod orders the slaughter of Bethlehem’s infants. Warned by an angel, Joseph flees by night with Mary and the child into Egypt, returning to Nazareth only after Herod’s death.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Out of Egypt have I called my son.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Teachers in the Temple
ENCOUNTERS.text: At twelve years old, Jesus stays behind after Passover. After three days of searching, Mary and Joseph find Him sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions — all astonished at His understanding.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?

ENCOUNTERS.name: John the Baptist
ENCOUNTERS.role: The voice crying in the wilderness
ENCOUNTERS.text: Clothed in camel’s hair, John calls Israel to repentance. When Jesus comes to be baptised, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice declares Him the beloved Son. Days later John points to Him and says the words that change everything.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Tempter
ENCOUNTERS.text: After forty days of fasting, Jesus is tempted three times — to turn stones to bread, to throw Himself from the temple, to bow for the kingdoms of the world. Each time He answers with the Word of God, and angels come to minister to Him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Andrew & John
ENCOUNTERS.text: Hearing John call Jesus the Lamb of God, two of his disciples follow Him. Jesus turns and asks what they seek. They spend the day with Him — and Andrew runs to find his brother.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Come and see.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Simon Peter
ENCOUNTERS.text: Andrew tells Simon, “We have found the Messias.” Jesus looks at him and gives him a new name — Cephas, the Rock — long before Simon is anything like a rock.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Philip
ENCOUNTERS.role: Of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter
ENCOUNTERS.text: The first disciple Jesus seeks out Himself, with two simple words. Philip immediately goes to find his friend.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Follow me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Nathanael
ENCOUNTERS.text: Sceptical — “Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?” — Nathanael is undone when Jesus reveals He saw him under the fig tree before Philip called him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Servants at Cana
ENCOUNTERS.text: At a wedding feast the wine runs out. Mary turns to the servants with the last recorded words she speaks in Scripture. Six stone jars are filled with water — and drawn out as the finest wine. His first sign.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Money Changers
ENCOUNTERS.text: At Passover, Jesus makes a scourge of small cords and drives out the sellers of oxen, sheep and doves, overturning the changers’ tables. Asked for a sign, He speaks of the temple of His body.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Nicodemus
ENCOUNTERS.role: A Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews
ENCOUNTERS.text: A respected teacher comes to Jesus under cover of darkness and hears that a man must be born again. In that quiet conversation, Jesus speaks the most beloved sentence in all of Scripture.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Woman at the Well
ENCOUNTERS.role: A Samaritan with five husbands behind her
ENCOUNTERS.text: At noon, alone, she comes to draw water — and a Jewish rabbi asks her for a drink. He knows everything she has ever done, and offers her living water. She leaves her waterpot and runs to tell the whole town.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Royal Official
ENCOUNTERS.role: A nobleman whose son lay dying
ENCOUNTERS.text: He walks twenty miles to beg Jesus to come before his son dies. Jesus sends him home with a word. On the road his servants meet him: the fever left at the very hour Jesus spoke.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Go thy way; thy son liveth.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The People of Nazareth
ENCOUNTERS.text: Handed the scroll of Isaiah, Jesus reads and declares, “This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.” Wonder turns to fury; they drive Him to the brow of a hill — but He passes through the midst of them.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter, Andrew, James & John
ENCOUNTERS.text: After a night of catching nothing, Peter lets down the nets at Jesus’ word — and they break with fish. Falling at His knees, Peter cries, “Depart from me; for I am a sinful man.” They leave everything and follow.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Man in the Synagogue
ENCOUNTERS.text: On the Sabbath a man cries out in the synagogue. With a word Jesus silences and expels the spirit, and His fame spreads through all Galilee.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Hold thy peace, and come out of him.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter’s Mother-in-Law
ENCOUNTERS.role: Lying sick with a great fever
ENCOUNTERS.text: Jesus takes her by the hand and lifts her up; the fever leaves at once. That evening the whole city gathers at the door, and He heals many.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Immediately she arose and ministered unto them.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Leper
ENCOUNTERS.text: Untouchable by law, he kneels and pleads. Moved with compassion, Jesus does the unthinkable — He reaches out and touches him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: I will; be thou clean.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Man Let Down Through the Roof
ENCOUNTERS.role: A paralytic carried by four friends
ENCOUNTERS.text: The house is too crowded, so his friends break open the roof and lower him down. Seeing their faith, Jesus first forgives his sins — then tells him to walk home.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Son, thy sins be forgiven thee… Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Matthew (Levi)
ENCOUNTERS.text: Despised as a collaborator with Rome, Matthew is sitting at the receipt of custom when Jesus says, “Follow me.” He rises, leaves all, and throws a feast for his fellow publicans and sinners.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Man at Bethesda
ENCOUNTERS.text: Among a great multitude of the blind, lame and withered, Jesus singles out one man who has no one to help him into the water. “Wilt thou be made whole?”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Man with the Withered Hand
ENCOUNTERS.role: In the synagogue on the Sabbath
ENCOUNTERS.text: With His critics watching, Jesus asks whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath. Grieved at their hardness of heart, He speaks — and the hand is restored whole as the other.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Stretch forth thine hand.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Twelve
ENCOUNTERS.text: After a night in prayer He names twelve: Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot — and Judas Iscariot.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: He ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Multitudes on the Mount
ENCOUNTERS.role: Disciples and crowds from every region
ENCOUNTERS.text: The greatest sermon ever preached: the Beatitudes, salt and light, love for enemies, the Lord’s Prayer, the lilies of the field, the house upon the rock. The people are astonished — He teaches as one having authority.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Centurion
ENCOUNTERS.role: A Roman officer whose servant was dying
ENCOUNTERS.text: A Gentile soldier asks only for a word, understanding authority better than Israel’s teachers. Jesus marvels: “I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Widow of Nain
ENCOUNTERS.text: At the city gate He meets a funeral procession. Seeing the mother, the Lord has compassion on her. He touches the bier, the bearers stand still, and the dead man sits up and begins to speak.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Weep not… Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Messengers of John
ENCOUNTERS.text: Imprisoned and perhaps doubting, John sends to ask, “Art thou he that should come?” Jesus answers not with a claim, but with evidence.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Woman with the Alabaster Box
ENCOUNTERS.role: A woman known as a sinner
ENCOUNTERS.text: Uninvited, she weeps at His feet, washing them with her tears and wiping them with her hair. To His scandalised host Jesus tells of two debtors, both forgiven — she loved much, for she was forgiven much.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Mary Magdalene, Joanna & Susanna
ENCOUNTERS.role: Women who ministered of their substance
ENCOUNTERS.text: Among those travelling with Him were women He had healed — Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils; Joanna, wife of Herod’s steward; Susanna, and many others who provided for Him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities…

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Blind and Mute Man
ENCOUNTERS.text: He heals the man so that he both speaks and sees. The crowds wonder, “Is not this the son of David?” — while the Pharisees accuse Him of casting out devils by Beelzebub.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: If I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.

ENCOUNTERS.name: His Mother and Brethren
ENCOUNTERS.text: Told that His family waits outside, Jesus stretches His hand toward His disciples and redefines what it means to belong to Him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Disciples in the Storm
ENCOUNTERS.role: Terrified on the Sea of Galilee
ENCOUNTERS.text: A great storm fills the boat with water while Jesus sleeps on a pillow in the stern. They wake Him — “Master, carest thou not that we perish?” He rebukes the wind, and there is a great calm.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Peace, be still.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Legion
ENCOUNTERS.role: The Gadarene demoniac among the tombs
ENCOUNTERS.text: No chain could hold him; he cut himself with stones night and day. Jesus casts the legion of spirits into a herd of swine — and the man is found sitting, clothed, in his right mind. He becomes the first missionary to the Decapolis.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Woman Who Touched His Hem
ENCOUNTERS.role: Twelve years with an issue of blood
ENCOUNTERS.text: She had spent all she had on physicians and only grew worse. In the press of the crowd she touches His garment and is healed instantly. Jesus stops everything to find her — and calls her daughter.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Jairus’ Daughter
ENCOUNTERS.role: Twelve years old, the ruler’s only daughter
ENCOUNTERS.text: News comes that the girl has died. “Be not afraid, only believe.” Putting the mourners out, Jesus takes her by the hand and speaks in Aramaic — and she rises and walks.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Talitha cumi… Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Two Blind Men
ENCOUNTERS.text: “Believe ye that I am able to do this?” “Yea, Lord.” He touches their eyes, and they are opened.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: According to your faith be it unto you.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Mute Man
ENCOUNTERS.text: When the devil is cast out, the dumb man speaks, and the multitudes marvel: “It was never so seen in Israel.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: It was never so seen in Israel.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Boy with Five Loaves
ENCOUNTERS.role: And a multitude of five thousand men
ENCOUNTERS.text: The only miracle recorded in all four Gospels. A boy offers his lunch; Jesus gives thanks and breaks it, and five thousand men — besides women and children — eat and are filled. Twelve baskets of fragments remain.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter on the Water
ENCOUNTERS.text: In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus comes walking on the sea. Peter asks to come to Him and walks on the water — until he sees the wind and begins to sink. Immediately Jesus stretches out His hand.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Sick of Gennesaret
ENCOUNTERS.text: Wherever He enters — villages, cities, country — they lay the sick in the streets and beg to touch even the border of His garment.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: As many as touched were made perfectly whole.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Crowd at Capernaum
ENCOUNTERS.text: They want another meal; He offers Himself. Many turn back and walk no more with Him. Jesus asks the Twelve, “Will ye also go away?” Peter answers for them all.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Syrophoenician Woman
ENCOUNTERS.text: She will not stop crying after Him for her tormented daughter. Tested, she answers with humble wit: even the dogs eat the crumbs from the master’s table. Her daughter is healed that very hour.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Deaf Man of Decapolis
ENCOUNTERS.role: With an impediment in his speech
ENCOUNTERS.text: Jesus takes him aside from the multitude, puts His fingers in his ears, touches his tongue, looks up to heaven, and sighs.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Four Thousand
ENCOUNTERS.role: Three days with Him in the wilderness
ENCOUNTERS.text: Moved with compassion for a hungry crowd far from home, He takes seven loaves and a few small fishes. All eat and are filled, and seven baskets remain.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: I have compassion on the multitude.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Blind Man of Bethsaida
ENCOUNTERS.text: Jesus leads him by the hand out of town. After the first touch he sees dimly; after the second, he sees every man clearly — the only healing that happens in stages.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: I see men as trees, walking.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter at Caesarea Philippi
ENCOUNTERS.text: “Whom say ye that I am?” Peter answers with a revelation not from flesh and blood. From this day Jesus begins to tell them plainly that He must suffer, die, and rise again.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Moses & Elijah
ENCOUNTERS.role: On the holy mountain, with Peter, James and John
ENCOUNTERS.text: His face shines as the sun, His garments white as light. The Law and the Prophets appear, speaking with Him of His departure at Jerusalem. A bright cloud overshadows them, and the Father speaks.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Father of the Afflicted Boy
ENCOUNTERS.role: His only son, seized by a spirit
ENCOUNTERS.text: The disciples could not help. “If thou canst believe, all things are possible.” The father’s tearful cry becomes the prayer of every struggling believer.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter and the Temple Tax
ENCOUNTERS.role: A coin in a fish’s mouth
ENCOUNTERS.text: Asked if his Master pays the temple tax, Peter is sent to cast a hook. The first fish he catches holds a piece of money — enough for them both.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Take that, and give unto them for me and thee.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Little Child
ENCOUNTERS.role: Set in the midst of the disciples
ENCOUNTERS.text: The disciples argue over who will be greatest. Jesus answers by calling a little child and setting him in the midst of them.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

ENCOUNTERS.name: James & John
ENCOUNTERS.text: When a Samaritan village refuses Him, the brothers offer to call down fire from heaven. He turns and rebukes them.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: The Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Would-Be Followers
ENCOUNTERS.text: One promises to follow anywhere; another must first bury his father; another must first say farewell. Jesus is honest about the cost.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Seventy
ENCOUNTERS.text: He sends seventy ahead of Him as lambs among wolves. They return with joy — even the devils are subject to them — and Jesus rejoices in spirit.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Lawyer
ENCOUNTERS.text: Seeking to justify himself, an expert in the Law receives a story: a man beaten on the Jericho road, passed by a priest and a Levite, rescued by a despised Samaritan.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Go, and do thou likewise.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Martha & Mary
ENCOUNTERS.text: Martha is cumbered about much serving; Mary sits at the Lord’s feet and hears His word. Jesus speaks tenderly to the busy sister.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Woman Taken in Adultery
ENCOUNTERS.text: Her accusers demand a verdict. Jesus stoops and writes on the ground. One by one, beginning at the eldest, they drop their stones and leave — until only Jesus and the woman remain.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Man Born Blind
ENCOUNTERS.role: A beggar who had never seen
ENCOUNTERS.text: Jesus spits on the ground, makes clay, anoints his eyes, and sends him to wash. Interrogated and cast out by the Pharisees, the man cannot explain theology — only his testimony. Later Jesus finds him, and he worships.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Woman Bent Double
ENCOUNTERS.text: She could in no wise lift herself up. Jesus calls her over, lays His hands on her, and immediately she is made straight and glorifies God.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Man with Dropsy
ENCOUNTERS.text: Watched closely on the Sabbath, Jesus asks the lawyers a question they cannot answer — then takes the man, heals him, and lets him go.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Publicans and Sinners
ENCOUNTERS.text: The Pharisees murmur that He receives sinners and eats with them. He answers with three stories of lost things — a sheep, a coin, and a son — and a father who runs.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: This my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Lazarus of Bethany
ENCOUNTERS.text: Jesus waits, and His friend dies. Martha meets Him with grief and faith; Mary falls at His feet. Jesus weeps. Then He stands before the tomb and cries with a loud voice — and the dead man comes forth, bound in grave clothes.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Ten Lepers
ENCOUNTERS.role: And the one Samaritan who returned
ENCOUNTERS.text: Ten cry out from a distance; all ten are cleansed on their way to the priests. Only one — a foreigner — turns back, falls on his face, and gives thanks.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Little Children
ENCOUNTERS.text: The disciples rebuke the parents. Jesus is much displeased — and takes the children up in His arms, puts His hands upon them, and blesses them.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Rich Young Ruler
ENCOUNTERS.text: He runs, kneels, and asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus, beholding him, loves him — and asks for the one thing he cannot give. He goes away grieved, for he had great possessions.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Mother of Zebedee’s Children
ENCOUNTERS.text: She asks that James and John sit at His right and left hand in His kingdom. Jesus answers by redefining greatness itself.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: The Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Blind Bartimaeus
ENCOUNTERS.role: Son of Timaeus, begging by the wayside
ENCOUNTERS.text: Told to be quiet, he cries out all the more. Jesus stands still and calls for him. Casting away his garment, he comes — and follows Jesus in the way.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me… Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Zacchaeus
ENCOUNTERS.role: Chief among the publicans, and rich
ENCOUNTERS.text: Too short to see over the crowd, he climbs a sycamore tree. Jesus stops beneath it, calls him by name, and invites Himself to dinner. Zacchaeus gives half his goods to the poor and restores fourfold.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Mary of Bethany
ENCOUNTERS.role: With a pound of costly spikenard
ENCOUNTERS.text: Six days before Passover she breaks the box and pours the ointment on Him, and the house is filled with its fragrance. Judas objects to the waste. Jesus says she has anointed Him for His burial.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: She hath wrought a good work on me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Crowds of Jerusalem
ENCOUNTERS.text: He rides into the city on a borrowed colt, fulfilling Zechariah’s prophecy, as the multitudes spread their garments in the way. Yet when He beholds the city, He weeps over it.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Hosanna; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Barren Fig Tree
ENCOUNTERS.text: A living parable. The tree He curses is found withered from the roots, and He teaches His disciples about faith and forgiveness in prayer.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Have faith in God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Blind and Lame in the Temple
ENCOUNTERS.text: Again He drives out the buyers and sellers. Then, in the cleared courts, the blind and the lame come to Him and He heals them, while children cry, “Hosanna to the son of David.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: My house shall be called the house of prayer.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Greeks
ENCOUNTERS.role: Gentiles come up to worship at the feast
ENCOUNTERS.text: Through Philip and Andrew they make a simple request. Jesus answers that the hour has come — and speaks of a grain of wheat.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Sir, we would see Jesus.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Pharisees & Herodians
ENCOUNTERS.text: “Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar?” He asks for a penny and whose image it bears. They marvel and leave Him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Scribe
ENCOUNTERS.role: Asking the first commandment of all
ENCOUNTERS.text: Love God with all thy heart, soul, mind and strength; love thy neighbour as thyself. The scribe answers discreetly, and Jesus tells him the most hopeful thing.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Thou art not far from the kingdom of God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Poor Widow
ENCOUNTERS.text: The rich cast in much. She casts in two small coins — all her living. Jesus calls His disciples to see what heaven sees.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: This poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Judas Iscariot
ENCOUNTERS.text: He covenants with the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver. At the table Jesus gives him the sop; Judas goes out immediately — “and it was night.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter at the Basin
ENCOUNTERS.text: Knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, the Lord rises, girds Himself with a towel, and washes His disciples’ feet. Peter protests: “Thou shalt never wash my feet.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Twelve at Table
ENCOUNTERS.text: He takes bread, gives thanks, breaks it; then the cup — the new testament in His blood. He gives them a new commandment, and they sing a hymn and go out to the Mount of Olives.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Thomas & Philip
ENCOUNTERS.text: “Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?” “Lord, shew us the Father.” The answers are among the most comforting words ever spoken.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter, James & John
ENCOUNTERS.text: Exceeding sorrowful unto death, He falls on His face and prays three times. His sweat is as great drops of blood; an angel appears to strengthen Him. Three times He returns to find His friends asleep.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Judas’ Kiss
ENCOUNTERS.role: With a band of soldiers and officers
ENCOUNTERS.text: The sign agreed upon is a kiss. When Jesus says “I am he,” the soldiers go backward and fall to the ground. He asks only that His disciples be let go. Then all forsake Him and flee.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?

ENCOUNTERS.name: Malchus
ENCOUNTERS.text: Peter draws a sword and cuts off his right ear. In the moment of His arrest, Jesus heals an enemy — His last miracle of healing before the cross.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: And he touched his ear, and healed him.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Young Man Who Fled
ENCOUNTERS.text: Recorded only by Mark: a young man follows, is seized, and escapes naked, leaving the linen behind. Many believe it was Mark himself.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: He left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Annas
ENCOUNTERS.role: Former high priest, father-in-law of Caiaphas
ENCOUNTERS.text: Questioned by night about His disciples and doctrine, Jesus replies that He spoke openly to the world. An officer strikes Him with the palm of his hand.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: If I have spoken well, why smitest thou me?

ENCOUNTERS.name: Caiaphas & the Council
ENCOUNTERS.text: False witnesses cannot agree. Finally the high priest asks Him directly — and Jesus answers. They condemn Him as guilty of death, spit in His face, and buffet Him.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? And Jesus said, I am.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter by the Fire
ENCOUNTERS.text: Three times he denies knowing Him. Then the cock crows — and the Lord turns and looks upon Peter. He goes out and weeps bitterly.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Judas’ Remorse
ENCOUNTERS.text: Seeing Jesus condemned, Judas brings back the thirty pieces, confessing he has betrayed innocent blood. The priests buy a potter’s field with it.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Pontius Pilate
ENCOUNTERS.text: “Art thou the King of the Jews?” Jesus answers that His kingdom is not of this world, and that He came to bear witness to the truth. Pilate finds no fault in Him — and washes his hands.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth?

ENCOUNTERS.name: Herod Antipas
ENCOUNTERS.text: Hoping to see a miracle, Herod questions Him at length. Jesus answers him nothing. Herod and his soldiers mock Him, array Him in a gorgeous robe, and send Him back to Pilate.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: He questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Pilate’s Wife
ENCOUNTERS.text: While her husband sits on the judgment seat, she sends an urgent message.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Barabbas
ENCOUNTERS.role: A notable prisoner, guilty of insurrection and murder
ENCOUNTERS.text: Offered a choice at the feast, the crowd chooses the guilty man. Barabbas walks free, and the innocent One dies in the place of the guilty.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Not this man, but Barabbas.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Soldiers
ENCOUNTERS.role: The whole band of the Praetorium
ENCOUNTERS.text: He is scourged. They plait a crown of thorns, put a purple robe on Him, and bow in mockery. Then Pilate brings Him out before the people.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Behold the man!

ENCOUNTERS.name: Simon of Cyrene
ENCOUNTERS.text: A man coming in from the country is compelled to carry the cross behind Jesus. Mark names his sons, as though his readers knew them well — the carrying may have changed his family forever.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: On him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Daughters of Jerusalem
ENCOUNTERS.text: Even on the way to His death, His concern is for others.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Thief on the Cross
ENCOUNTERS.text: One criminal rails on Him. The other rebukes his companion and makes a simple request: “Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.” He is the last person Jesus saves before He dies.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

ENCOUNTERS.name: His Mother & the Beloved Disciple
ENCOUNTERS.text: Simeon’s sword has reached her soul. From the cross Jesus entrusts His mother to John, and from that hour the disciple takes her unto his own home.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Woman, behold thy son!… Behold thy mother!

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Centurion at the Cross
ENCOUNTERS.text: Seeing how He cried out and gave up the ghost, the Roman officer in charge of the execution becomes the first to confess Him after His death.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Truly this man was the Son of God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Women Who Watched
ENCOUNTERS.role: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, Salome
ENCOUNTERS.text: When the men had fled, the women stayed — beholding afar off, and afterward marking where He was laid.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: There were also women looking on afar off.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Joseph of Arimathea & Nicodemus
ENCOUNTERS.place: A new tomb in a garden
ENCOUNTERS.text: A rich counsellor begs Pilate for the body. Nicodemus — who first came by night — brings a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes. They wrap Him in linen and lay Him in a tomb where never man was laid. A great stone is rolled to the door.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: There laid they Jesus.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Women at the Tomb
ENCOUNTERS.text: Very early, as it begins to dawn, they wonder who will roll away the stone. There is a great earthquake. An angel sits upon the stone, his countenance like lightning — and speaks the words that changed the world.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter & John
ENCOUNTERS.text: They run together; John outruns Peter. Inside, the linen clothes lie in their place, and the napkin that was about His head folded by itself. The other disciple sees — and believes.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: So they ran both together.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Mary Magdalene
ENCOUNTERS.text: She thinks He is the gardener — until He speaks her name. The first person to see the risen Lord is a woman once possessed by seven devils, sent as the apostle to the apostles.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Cleopas & His Companion
ENCOUNTERS.text: A stranger joins them on the road and opens the Scriptures, beginning at Moses. At supper He takes bread, blesses and breaks it — and their eyes are opened. He vanishes from their sight.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Disciples Behind Closed Doors
ENCOUNTERS.text: The doors are shut, yet Jesus stands in the midst. He shows them His hands and side, eats broiled fish before them, and breathes on them the Holy Ghost.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Thomas
ENCOUNTERS.text: “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails… I will not believe.” Eight days later, Jesus invites him to reach out his hand. The doubter makes the highest confession in the Gospels.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: My Lord and my God.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Seven Disciples at Dawn
ENCOUNTERS.text: A figure on the shore tells them where to cast. The net fills with a hundred and fifty-three great fish, yet is not broken. “It is the Lord!” Peter plunges into the sea. Breakfast is waiting on a fire of coals. His last recorded miracle.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find.

ENCOUNTERS.name: Peter Restored
ENCOUNTERS.text: Beside another charcoal fire, three questions answer three denials. Grieved, Peter says, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee.”
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Feed my sheep.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Beloved Disciple
ENCOUNTERS.role: Who leaned on His breast at supper
ENCOUNTERS.text: Peter asks what will happen to John. Jesus’ answer is for every disciple who has ever compared their path to another’s.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: What is that to thee? follow thou me.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Eleven on the Mountain
ENCOUNTERS.text: All power is given unto Him in heaven and in earth. He sends them to make disciples of all nations — with a promise that has never expired.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.

ENCOUNTERS.name: The Witnesses of the Ascension
ENCOUNTERS.text: He leads them out as far as Bethany, lifts up His hands, and blesses them. While He blesses them, He is parted from them and a cloud receives Him. Two men in white apparel promise He will come again in like manner. They return to Jerusalem with great joy.
ENCOUNTERS.quote: While he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.

LAST_WORDS.t: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Woman, behold thy son! … Behold thy mother!
Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? — My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

I_AM.line: He that cometh to me shall never hunger.
He that followeth me shall not walk in darkness.
By me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.
The good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
He that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.

I_AM.t: the way, the truth, and the life
I_AM.line: No man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
I am the vine, ye are the branches.

SAINT_ERAS.title: Before all ages
SAINT_ERAS.text: Before the first saint walked the earth, there were the angels: spirits made by God, who “do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.” One of them the Church has honoured above all the rest.
SAINT_ERAS.also: Scripture names two other archangels: Gabriel, who came to Mary, and Raphael, who walked with Tobias. And beside every child, said Jesus, stands an angel of their own (Matthew 18:10).

SAINT_ERAS.title: The first centuries
SAINT_ERAS.text: From a carpenter’s house in Nazareth to the arenas of Rome and the libraries of North Africa: the Church is born, persecuted, and learns to think.
SAINT_ERAS.also: Also of these years: Stephen, Agnes, Lucy, Cecilia, Ambrose, Jerome.

SAINT_ERAS.title: The Middle Ages
SAINT_ERAS.text: Cathedrals rise and universities are founded, and God raises up beggars and preachers, a scholar, a mystic, a shepherd girl, an invalid and a widow to renew His Church.
SAINT_ERAS.also: In the long centuries before them: Benedict, Patrick, Gregory the Great, Bede, Bernard, Dominic.

SAINT_ERAS.title: Reform and mission
SAINT_ERAS.text: The Church is torn and renewed while ships open the world. Saints reform it from within, win hearts back with gentleness, and carry the Gospel to India, Japan — and Sri Lanka.
SAINT_ERAS.also: Also of these years: John of the Cross, Philip Neri, Rose of Lima, Vincent de Paul, Martin de Porres, Peter Claver.

SAINT_ERAS.title: Our own times
SAINT_ERAS.text: Saints with photographs. They lived in a world of trains, wars, cameras and microphones — a world very like ours.
SAINT_ERAS.also: Also of these years: Josephine Bakhita, Gianna Beretta Molla, Óscar Romero, Carlo Acutis.

SAINTS.name: Michael
SAINTS.title: Who Is Like God?
SAINTS.patron: Soldiers, police, the sick and the dying, and the whole Church
story: Michael is not a man or woman who became holy. He is an archangel — a spirit created by God before the world began — and one of only three angels whom Scripture calls by name. His name is a question in Hebrew: Mi-ka-El, “Who is like God?” The Book of Daniel calls him “the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people,” the guardian of God’s people in their darkest hour.

The last book of the Bible shows him at war: “There was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon.” The Church’s ancient tradition tells the story behind it — that when the proudest of the angels refused to serve God, Michael answered with his own name: Who is like God? Yet in the Letter of Jude, even when he contends with the devil, he does not insult him; he says only, “The Lord rebuke thee.” His strength is not his own. It is the strength of someone who knows exactly who God is — and who he is not.
moments: The prophet Daniel
Named as the great prince who stands guard over God’s people in their time of trouble.
Daniel 12:1
The body of Moses
Contends with the devil, yet will not curse him: “The Lord rebuke thee.”
Jude 1:9
War in heaven
Leads the angels against the dragon, “that old serpent,” and casts him down.
Revelation 12:7–9
Monte Gargano, c. 490
Appears in a mountain cave in southern Italy, which becomes one of the great shrines of Europe.
Tradition
Rome, 590
As plague ravages the city, Pope Gregory’s procession sees him sheathe his sword above Hadrian’s tomb — ever since called Castel Sant’Angelo.
Tradition
Pope Leo XIII adds a prayer to Saint Michael to the prayers said after every Low Mass.

quote.t: Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle; be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil.

end.text: Angels do not die, so Michael’s chapter has no last page. Scripture shows him at the end of all things, still standing up for God’s people. The Church has honoured him since the earliest centuries, and in the old tradition he is the angel who comes to the dying, to bring their souls safely home.

lessons.d: Michael’s whole name points away from himself: Who is like God? The proud angel said “I.” Michael said “God.” Every victory over evil starts there.
Even facing the devil, he would not trade insults: “The Lord rebuke thee.” We can stand firmly against what is wrong without hatred in our mouths.
Scripture says the battle against evil is real — and that heaven is not neutral in it. When temptation is strong, call for help. It comes.

SAINTS.practice: Pray the prayer to Saint Michael tonight before you sleep — for yourself, and for someone you know who is struggling against something stronger than them.

SAINTS.name: Anne
SAINTS.title: The Grandmother of Jesus
SAINTS.patron: Mothers, grandparents, and couples longing for a child
story: Scripture never names Mary’s parents. Their names come from a very early Christian writing, the Protoevangelium of James, from the second century — and the Church has loved them ever since. Anne and her husband Joachim, it says, were devout and generous, giving a share of everything they had to the Temple and the poor. But they had no child, and in their world that was a grief people whispered about. When Joachim brought his offering to the Temple, he was turned away for being childless.

Joachim went out into the wilderness to fast and pray for forty days. Anne, at home, mourned. Then she went into her garden, sat beneath a laurel tree, and saw a sparrows’ nest full of young. She wept: even the birds are fruitful before you, O Lord. An angel came to her, and to Joachim in the desert, with the same message: you will have a child, and she will be spoken of in all the world. The two ran to meet each other at the gate of Jerusalem. Their daughter was Mary. Anne promised her to God — and, in a scene painters have loved for centuries, taught her to read the Scriptures.
moments: The Temple
Joachim’s offering is refused because the couple have no child. He goes into the desert to fast and pray.
Tradition
The laurel tree
Anne, grieving in her garden, sees a nest of young sparrows and pours out her heart to God. An angel promises her a child.
Tradition
The gate
Anne and Joachim, each told by an angel, run to meet each other at the gate of Jerusalem.
Tradition
Mary
Their daughter is born, and Anne keeps her promise to give her to God.
Tradition
Age three
They bring the little girl to the Temple, where she dances on the altar steps.
Tradition

quote.t: For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him.

end.text: Nothing certain is known of her death. Tradition pictures her, like Joseph, dying with Jesus and Mary beside her. Her name, Hannah in Hebrew, means “grace.” Churches in her honour rose in Constantinople in the sixth century, and in Jerusalem over the house where Mary was said to be born, beside the Pool of Bethesda. In Sri Lanka, pilgrims in their tens of thousands keep her feast on the shore at Talawila.

lessons.d: Anne did not pretend she was fine. She took her grief into the garden and told God exactly how it felt. Honest prayer is still prayer.
The answer came late, and it was greater than anything she had asked for: not only a child, but the mother of the Saviour.
Every Christian learned to pray from someone. Anne taught Mary, and Mary taught Jesus. Grandparents and parents shape saints.

SAINTS.practice: Call or visit a grandparent or an elderly person this week. Thank them for something they taught you — or ask them how they learned to pray.

SAINTS.name: Joseph
SAINTS.title: The Silent Guardian
SAINTS.from: Nazareth, of the house of David
SAINTS.patron: The whole Church, fathers, workers, and a happy death
story: Scripture never records a single word from Joseph. It records what he did. A carpenter of Nazareth, descended from King David, he was engaged to Mary when he learned she was with child — and not by him. He was a just man, and he decided to end the engagement quietly, to spare her public shame.

Then an angel spoke to him in a dream, and Joseph rose and did exactly what he was told. Four times God spoke to him in dreams, and four times he obeyed at once: taking Mary as his wife, fleeing by night to Egypt, coming home, settling in Nazareth. He gave Jesus his name, his trade and his home. The Son of God learned to work wood with Joseph’s hands guiding His.
moments: Before the birth
Learns Mary is with child and resolves to protect her quietly — then obeys the angel and takes her home.
Matthew 1:18–24
Bethlehem
Finds no room at the inn, and keeps watch over the newborn Child.
Luke 2:4–7
By night
Warned in a dream, takes the Child and His mother and flees to Egypt before Herod’s soldiers come.
Matthew 2:13–15
The Temple
Searches three days for the twelve-year-old Jesus: “thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.”
Nazareth
Teaches Jesus his trade. The town would later call Him “the carpenter’s son.”
Matthew 13:55

quote.t: Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him.

end.how: Died before Jesus began His ministry
end.text: Joseph is never mentioned after the finding in the Temple, and from the cross Jesus entrusts His mother to John — so Joseph had almost certainly died by then. Tradition pictures him dying in the arms of Jesus and Mary, which is why he is the patron of a happy death.

lessons.t: Let your life do the talking
lessons.d: Joseph is remembered for what he did, not for anything he said. Faithfulness rarely makes noise. It shows up, keeps its promises and does the next right thing.
Before any angel spoke, Joseph had already chosen mercy: he would not shame Mary, even when he thought she had wronged him. Justice and kindness are not opposites.

lessons.t: Obey quickly, even in the dark
lessons.d: Joseph was never given the whole plan — only the next step, usually at night. He got up and went. God most often guides us one step at a time.

SAINTS.practice: Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for — and tell no one.

SAINTS.name: Agatha
SAINTS.title: Not for Sale
SAINTS.patron: Sicily, nurses, women with breast cancer, and protection from fire
story: Agatha was a young Christian woman of a noble family in Sicily, who had promised her life to God. Her name, in Greek, means “good.” During the persecution of the emperor Decius, the Roman governor Quintianus wanted her — for her beauty and for her fortune. When she refused him, he used the law against Christians to break her. He had her handed over for a month to a woman who kept a brothel, hoping to destroy her will. She came out unchanged.

Then he had her tortured, and ordered that her breasts be cut away — which is why painters show her carrying them on a plate, and why women facing breast cancer ask her prayers today. The old account says that in the night Saint Peter came to her in prison and healed her wounds. Quintianus had her rolled on burning coals, and she died in her cell, praying, around the year 251. A year later Mount Etna erupted, and the people of Catania carried her veil from her tomb against the lava — which, they said, stopped.
moments: Catania
Promises her life to God, and refuses the governor Quintianus.
Tradition
Arrested
Under the persecution of Decius, she is handed over to a brothel to break her will. She stays steadfast.
Tradition
Prison
Mutilated on the governor’s orders; in the night, Saint Peter comes and heals her.
Tradition
The coals
Rolled on burning coals, she dies in her cell, praying.
Tradition
When Etna erupts, the people carry her veil against the lava, and the city is spared.
Tradition

quote.t: Jesus Christ, Lord of all, you see my heart, you know my desires. Possess all that I am. I am your sheep: make me worthy to overcome the devil.
quote.r: Her prayer, from the early accounts

end.text: Within a few centuries her name was in the oldest prayer of the Mass, the Roman Canon, where it is still read beside Lucy, Agnes and Cecilia. Every February Catania carries her relics through its streets for three days, in one of the largest religious processions in the world.

lessons.t: Your dignity is not for sale
lessons.d: Agatha was offered safety, wealth and a powerful husband — at the price of her faith and her body. She said no. No one has the right to own you.

lessons.t: What others do to you does not define you
lessons.d: They tried to degrade her, and could not touch who she was. Wounds done to us, even shameful ones, are not who we are. God sees the whole person.
For centuries women facing illness have asked her prayers. Suffering that once seemed hidden can be carried together.

SAINTS.practice: Pray today for a woman you know who is ill or waiting for frightening news — and send her a message to let her know she is not alone.

SAINTS.name: Sebastian
SAINTS.title: The Soldier Who Stood Twice
SAINTS.from: Gaul or Milan; served in Rome
SAINTS.patron: Soldiers, athletes, and the sick in times of plague
story: Sebastian was an officer of the imperial guard in Rome under the emperor Diocletian, the fiercest persecutor the early Church ever faced. He kept his faith hidden — not out of fear, the story says, but so that he could stay close to the Christians in prison and strengthen them before they died.

When he was found out, Diocletian felt betrayed. He had Sebastian tied to a stake, shot with arrows by his own soldiers, and left for dead. But a Christian widow named Irene came at night to take his body for burial and found him still breathing. She nursed him back to health. Instead of fleeing Rome, Sebastian went and stood where the emperor would pass, and told him to his face to stop killing Christians. This time Diocletian had him beaten to death.
moments: Rome
Serves in the emperor’s guard while secretly strengthening Christian prisoners.
Tradition
The arrows
Discovered, he is shot with arrows and left for dead.
Tradition
Irene
A widow comes to bury him, finds him alive, and nurses him back to health.
Tradition
The second stand
Healed, he confronts the emperor in public instead of hiding.
Tradition

quote.t: Take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.

end.text: His body was thrown into the great sewer of Rome, then recovered by Christians and buried in the catacombs on the Appian Way, where the Basilica of San Sebastiano stands today. Artists have painted the arrows for centuries; it is easy to forget that he survived them — and went back.

lessons.t: Be faithful where you are posted
lessons.d: Sebastian did not leave the army to be holy; he was holy in the army. Your office, classroom or shop may be exactly where your faith is needed most.

lessons.t: Being knocked down is not the end
lessons.d: The arrows did not finish him. Whatever has wounded you, God can raise you up again — often through someone like Irene.
Surviving once is brave. Walking back to face what hurt you, for the sake of others, is braver still.

SAINTS.practice: Find one person who is being worn down — at work, at school or at home — and stand with them today.

SAINTS.name: Catherine of Alexandria
SAINTS.title: The Philosopher Martyr
SAINTS.patron: Students, philosophers, librarians and young women
story: Catherine, the story goes, was a young noblewoman of Alexandria in Egypt — the greatest city of learning in the ancient world — brilliant, beautiful and fiercely well read. She became a Christian as a teenager, and gave her whole heart to Christ. When the emperor Maxentius came to Alexandria and ordered everyone to sacrifice to the gods, Catherine, about eighteen, went to the emperor in person and told him he was wrong.

Unable to answer her, the emperor summoned fifty of his best philosophers to debate her. She did not lose. By the end, the story says, all fifty had become Christians — and were put to death for it. The emperor’s wife and the captain of his guard were won over too. Maxentius had a machine of spiked wheels built to tear her apart; when she touched it, it shattered. In the end she was beheaded. Monks later said that angels carried her body to Mount Sinai, where the monastery that bears her name still stands.
moments: Alexandria
A young scholar of the great city, she is baptised and gives her life to Christ.
Tradition
Before the emperor
Confronts Maxentius over the persecution of Christians.
Tradition
Fifty philosophers
Debates the empire’s wisest men — and they are converted.
Tradition
The wheel
Bound to a spiked wheel, which shatters at her touch.
Tradition
Sinai
Her relics are honoured at the monastery at the foot of Mount Sinai.
Tradition

quote.t: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

end.text: Her story comes from accounts written centuries later, and historians are unsure how much of it is fact; for that reason the Church took her feast out of the universal calendar in 1969 — and, so loved had she remained, restored it in 2002. Joan of Arc said Catherine was one of the voices who spoke to her. The spinning firework called a Catherine wheel is named after the wheel that broke.

lessons.d: Catherine did not leave her intelligence at the church door. Study, questions and good arguments can all be offered to God.
She did not hide in her library. She walked into the emperor’s presence on behalf of Christians who were being killed.

lessons.t: Wisdom is a gift — ask for it
lessons.d: “I will give you a mouth and wisdom.” Before a hard conversation, an exam or an interview, ask the Holy Spirit for the right words.

SAINTS.practice: Before your next exam, interview or difficult conversation, pray: “Lord, give me a mouth and wisdom.” Then go in peace.

SAINTS.name: Helena
SAINTS.title: The Empress Who Found the Cross
SAINTS.patron: Converts, archaeologists, and those in difficult marriages
story: Helena was born to a humble family — Saint Ambrose called her a stable-girl. She caught the eye of a Roman officer named Constantius, and bore him a son, Constantine. When Constantius rose towards the throne, he put her aside to marry the emperor’s stepdaughter, a more useful match. Helena lived for years in the shadows, a discarded woman.

Then her son became emperor. In 312 Constantine won the Battle of the Milvian Bridge under the sign of the cross, and the next year he made it legal to be a Christian across the empire. Helena, too, became a Christian — late in life. Honoured now as empress, she spent her wealth on the poor, freed prisoners, and in her late seventies made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land. There she had churches built at Bethlehem and on the Mount of Olives, and, tradition says, she searched for the cross of Christ — and found it near Calvary, where the Church of the Holy Sepulchre was built.
moments: Youth
A stable-girl, by Ambrose’s account, who marries a Roman officer and bears a son, Constantine.
Set aside by her husband so that he can make a more useful marriage.
Her son wins at the Milvian Bridge under the sign of the cross, and makes Christianity legal.
Later life
Becomes a Christian; gives generously to the poor and to prisoners.
Pilgrimage to the Holy Land; churches rise at Bethlehem and on the Mount of Olives.
Jerusalem
Finds the cross of Christ near Calvary.
Tradition

quote.t: But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

end.how: Died in peace, with her son beside her
end.text: Eusebius, who knew Constantine, wrote that she died with her son at her side. Her body was carried to Rome, and her great porphyry coffin is in the Vatican Museums. Pieces of the wood she found were sent across the Christian world; ever since, the Church has kept 14 September as the feast of the Holy Cross.

lessons.t: Rejection is not the end of your story
lessons.d: Helena was set aside by the man she loved, for political gain. Decades later she was one of the most honoured women in the world — and, far more, a saint.

lessons.t: It is never too late to begin
lessons.d: She became a Christian late in life, and did her greatest work in her seventies. God has not finished with anyone yet.
Helena went looking for the wood of the cross. We find it closer to home: in suffering offered with love, and in the people around us who carry heavy things.

SAINTS.practice: Make the sign of the cross slowly each time you pray today — and offer Christ one heavy thing you are carrying.

SAINTS.name: Nicholas
SAINTS.title: The Secret Giver
SAINTS.patron: Children, sailors, the poor and the falsely accused
story: Nicholas was born to wealthy Christian parents in what is now Turkey, and was orphaned young. He took Jesus at His word — “sell that ye have, and give alms” — and set about giving his inheritance away, quietly.

The best-loved story: a man in his town had lost everything and had three daughters with no dowry, which meant they could not marry and might be sold. Nicholas came at night and threw a bag of gold through the window, then slipped away. He did it a second time, then a third — and the father, waiting up, caught him. Nicholas begged him to tell no one. He became bishop of Myra, was imprisoned for his faith under Diocletian, and was remembered as a fierce defender of the poor and the wrongly condemned.
moments: Youth
Orphaned, he gives away his inheritance to people in need.
Tradition
Three nights
Throws gold through a poor man’s window so that his daughters need not be sold.
Tradition
Myra
Chosen as bishop; imprisoned for the faith, then freed.
Tradition
Justice
Stops the execution of three innocent men by catching hold of the executioner’s sword.
Tradition

quote.t: When thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: that thine alms may be in secret.

end.text: In 1087 sailors carried his relics to Bari in Italy, where they rest today. In the Netherlands he became Sinterklaas, who leaves gifts in children’s shoes; in America, Sinterklaas became Santa Claus. Behind the red suit is a bishop who gave in secret.

lessons.t: Give where it can’t be seen
lessons.d: Nicholas ran so that he would not be thanked. Generosity that needs an audience is still a kind of buying.
The gold did more than feed a family — it saved three young women from being sold. Ask not only what people need, but what they are afraid of.
The man who slipped gifts through windows also seized an executioner’s sword. Kindness is not weakness.

SAINTS.practice: Give something away anonymously this week — money, a meal, someone’s bill — and let no one find out.

SAINTS.name: Monica
SAINTS.title: The Mother Who Never Gave Up
SAINTS.feast: 27 August — the day before her son’s
SAINTS.patron: Mothers, wives in hard marriages, and parents of children who have left the faith
story: Monica was a Christian girl of North Africa, married young to Patricius, a pagan official with a quick temper and a wandering eye, and she shared a house with a mother-in-law who disliked her. Other wives in the town came to her with bruised faces; Monica, Augustine later wrote, had none, because she had learned to let her husband’s anger pass in silence and to speak to him once he was calm. Over the years her patience won over her mother-in-law — and in the end her husband, who was baptised shortly before he died.

Her eldest son broke her heart. Augustine was brilliant and restless; he abandoned the faith, lived with a woman he did not marry, and joined a sect. For years Monica wept and prayed for him. When she begged a bishop to talk sense into him, he answered, “Go now; it is not possible that the son of these tears should perish.” When Augustine sailed secretly for Rome to escape her, she followed him over the sea, to Rome and then to Milan. There, after years of tears, she saw him baptised at Easter 387.
moments: Thagaste
Married to Patricius, a hot-tempered pagan; she wins him and his mother over by patience.
Confessions IX.9
Patricius is baptised before he dies; Monica is left a widow with three children.
Years of tears
Augustine leaves the faith. A bishop tells her: “The son of these tears shall not perish.”
Confessions III.12
Augustine sails for Rome by night, leaving her praying on the shore. She follows him to Italy.
Confessions V.8
Easter 387
Sees her son baptised by Ambrose in Milan.
Confessions IX.6
Ostia
At a window overlooking a garden, mother and son speak together of heaven.
Confessions IX.10

quote.t: Nothing is far from God, and I need not fear that He will not know where to find me at the end of the world, to raise me up.

end.how: Died of a fever, at peace
end.text: Waiting for a ship home to Africa, she fell ill. She told her sons not to worry about where she would be buried: “Lay this body anywhere. Only remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you are.” Augustine, who had made her weep for so long, wept for her, and wrote her story into his Confessions. In 1945 two boys digging a hole in Ostia uncovered a piece of her original gravestone. Her relics rest in Rome, in the church of Sant’Agostino.

lessons.t: Never stop praying for your children
lessons.d: Years passed without any sign of change. Monica kept praying anyway, and lived to see her son baptised. No prayer for someone you love is wasted.
She did not win over her difficult husband and mother-in-law with arguments. She won them with gentleness — and by choosing the right moment to speak.
She could not make Augustine believe. She stayed near him, loved him, and let God do what only God can do.

SAINTS.practice: Name the person you most want to come closer to God. Pray for them by name every day this week — and do one kind thing for them without mentioning faith at all.

SAINTS.name: Augustine
SAINTS.title: The Restless Heart
SAINTS.patron: Theologians, and everyone who is searching
story: Augustine was brilliant, ambitious and restless. His mother Monica was a devout Christian; he was not. As a student in Carthage he chased pleasure and success, lived for fifteen years with a woman he never married, fathered a son, and joined a fashionable sect. He later confessed that he used to pray, “Give me chastity — but not yet.”

Monica never stopped praying. She wept for him so often that a bishop finally told her, “It is not possible that the son of these tears should perish.” She followed him across the sea to Italy. In Milan, Augustine heard Bishop Ambrose preach and could not shake it off. One day in a garden, in anguish, he heard a child’s voice chanting, “Take and read, take and read.” He opened Paul’s letter to the Romans and read: “Put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ.” He was baptised at Easter 387. Monica died a few months later, at peace. He became a bishop and one of the greatest minds the Church has known.
moments: Carthage
Chases pleasure, success and philosophy after philosophy — and is never satisfied.
Confessions III
Monica’s tears
His mother prays for him for years; a bishop promises her he will not be lost.
Confessions III.12
Milan, 386
In a garden he hears “Take and read,” opens Romans 13 and surrenders.
Confessions VIII.12
Easter 387
Baptised by Ambrose, together with his son Adeodatus.
Confessions IX.6
Hippo
Made bishop; writes the Confessions and The City of God.

quote.t: You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.

end.how: Died of fever, praying the psalms
end.text: He died while the Vandals besieged his city, with the penitential psalms written on the wall beside his bed so he could read them as he lay dying. His mother had asked only one thing before her own death: “Remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you may be.”

lessons.d: Augustine was thirty-two, with a past he was ashamed of, when he turned to God. Grace is not limited by how far you have wandered.
Monica prayed for years without seeing a change. Her tears were not wasted. Keep praying for the one you love who is far from God.
The emptiness that pleasure, money and success cannot fill is not a flaw in you. It is a hunger for God.

SAINTS.practice: Write the name of someone far from God on a slip of paper, keep it in your wallet, and pray for them each time you see it.

SAINTS.name: Francis
SAINTS.title: The Little Poor Man
SAINTS.patron: Italy, animals and the natural world, and peace
story: Francis was the son of a rich cloth merchant — the life of every party in Assisi, dreaming of glory as a knight. War gave him a year in a prison cell instead, and a long illness after it. Riding out one day, he met a leper. He had always been disgusted by lepers; this time he got down from his horse and kissed the man’s hand.

Praying in the ruined chapel of San Damiano, he heard the crucifix speak: “Francis, go and repair my house, which, as you see, is falling into ruin.” He took it literally, sold his father’s cloth to pay for stones, and was dragged before the bishop. There, in the square, he took off every piece of clothing he wore and handed it back. “Until now I have called you my father on earth. From now on I can say: Our Father, who art in heaven.” He lived the rest of his life with nothing — and with a joy that drew thousands after him.
moments: Kisses a leper; hears the crucifix of San Damiano say, “Repair my house.”
Gives back even his clothes to his father before the bishop of Assisi.
With his first brothers, receives the Pope’s blessing on a life of poverty.
Crosses the battle lines of the Crusade to speak with the Sultan of Egypt in peace.
Makes the first Christmas crib, at Greccio.
Receives the wounds of Christ in his hands, feet and side on Mount La Verna.

quote.t: When I was in sin, it seemed too bitter to me to see lepers. And the Lord himself led me among them, and I showed mercy to them. And when I left them, what had seemed bitter to me was turned into sweetness of soul and body.

end.how: Died singing, lying on the bare earth
end.text: Nearly blind and in great pain, he asked to be laid on the bare ground. He had added a last verse to his Canticle of the Creatures — “Praised be you, my Lord, through our Sister Bodily Death” — and he died while the brothers sang it. He was declared a saint two years later. In 2013, for the first time, a pope took his name.

lessons.d: Francis found that the less he owned, the freer he was to love. What we possess can quietly begin to possess us.
The leper he dreaded became the beginning of his joy. Sometimes God is waiting in the very place we avoid.
Brother Sun, Sister Moon, Sister Water: Francis saw the world as the gift of one Father, to be cared for, not used up.

SAINTS.practice: Give away one thing you own but do not need — and spend five minutes outdoors today thanking God for something He made.

SAINTS.name: Anthony
SAINTS.title: The Hidden Preacher
SAINTS.patron: Lost things, the poor and travellers
story: Fernando was born in Lisbon to a noble family and became a learned young priest. In 1220 the bodies of five Franciscan friars, martyred in Morocco, were carried through his city. Moved, he joined the Franciscans, took the name Anthony, and sailed for Morocco to give his own life. Instead he fell gravely ill, and on the voyage home a storm drove his ship to Sicily.

Unknown and unwell, he was sent to a small hermitage in Italy, where he prayed and washed dishes. No one guessed what he knew. Then, at an ordination where no one had prepared to preach, his superior told him to say something. He spoke — and the room was stunned. From then on crowds of thousands followed him through Italy and France; shops closed when he came to town. Francis himself asked him to teach the brothers. When the people of Rimini refused to listen, the story goes, he went down to the shore and preached to the fish — and they lifted their heads from the water to hear.
moments: Moved by five martyred friars, becomes a Franciscan and sets out for Morocco.
Shipwrecked in Sicily; sent to a hermitage, unknown.
Ordered to preach without preparation — and his gift is discovered.
Rimini
Ignored by the people, he preaches to the fish on the shore.
Tradition
The psalter
A novice runs off with his treasured book of psalms; Anthony prays, and the young man brings it back — which is why he is the saint of lost things.
Tradition

quote.t: Actions speak louder than words; let your words teach and your actions speak.

end.text: Worn out at thirty-five, he asked to be taken to Padua. His last words were, “I see my Lord.” As the news spread, children ran through the streets crying, “The saint is dead!” He was declared a saint less than a year later — one of the fastest canonisations in history.

lessons.t: Be faithful in the hidden years
lessons.d: Anthony washed dishes in obscurity while carrying a gift no one knew about. God sees the kitchen years. Nothing done faithfully is wasted.
He set out to die a martyr in Africa and became a preacher in Italy. A shipwreck can be a new beginning.
His sermons moved crowds because his life matched them. The best argument for faith is a life that looks like Jesus.

SAINTS.practice: The next time you lose something, ask St Anthony’s help — and while you search, pray for someone who has lost their way, their faith or their hope.

SAINTS.name: Clare
SAINTS.title: The Light of Assisi
SAINTS.patron: Television, embroiderers, and those with eye disease
story: Clare — her name means “bright” — was the eldest daughter of a noble family of Assisi, some twelve years younger than Francis. When she heard him preach, she knew she wanted the same poverty and the same joy. On the night of Palm Sunday 1212, at eighteen, she slipped out of her family’s house and ran down to the little chapel of the Portiuncula, where Francis and his brothers met her with torches, and there he cut off her long hair. Her family came to drag her home; she clung to the altar and showed them her shorn head. They left without her.
